aspects.description: Mini Test Projects are in separate self-contained folders A1, A2, A3, B1, B2, B3, C1, and C2
aspects.extraDescription: Test: Open the submission root. Confirm folders A1, A2, A3, B1, B2, B3, C1, and C2 exist, each holds that mini Test Project’s files, and there are no extra unrelated mini-project folders.

aspects.description: At least one git commit exists for each of the eight mini Test Projects
aspects.extraDescription: Test: Run git log --oneline in the submission. Pass if there is at least one commit attributable to each of A1, A2, A3, B1, B2, B3, C1, and C2 (message and/or changed paths).

aspects.description: Git commit messages are readable and easy to understand
judgementScoreDescription: Commit messages are missing, one-word placeholders such as “update”, or do not describe the change.
Messages are short single lines that name the mini Test Project but do not explain what was implemented.
Messages name the mini Test Project and the change, but wording is vague, repeated, or hard to follow without reading the diff.
Each relevant commit has a clear subject (and body if needed) so a reader can tell what was implemented without opening the diff.

aspects.description: Index page links to every mini Test Project
aspects.extraDescription: Test: Open index.html in Google Chrome. Follow each link and confirm A1, A2, A3, B1, B2, B3, C1, and C2 load (C1 and C2 may require php -S from that folder or the submission root).

aspects.description: Index page shows a thumbnail for each mini Test Project
aspects.extraDescription: Test: On the index page, each of the eight mini Test Projects has a visible thumbnail image or graphic preview.

aspects.description: Index page shows a title for each mini Test Project
aspects.extraDescription: Test: On the index page, each of the eight mini Test Projects has a readable title (for example Floating Label, Turntable).

aspects.description: Empty unfocused input shows the label inside the field
aspects.extraDescription: Test: Open A1 in Chrome. With the field empty and not focused, the label sits inside the input, matching assets/A1/input.mp4. No JavaScript is required.

aspects.description: On focus the label moves to the top edge and becomes smaller
aspects.extraDescription: Test: Click or tab into the empty input. The label animates to the top edge of the field, becomes smaller, and changes colour. HTML/CSS only.

aspects.description: Label stays floating after blur when the input contains text
aspects.extraDescription: Test: Type text, then click outside the field. The label remains in the floating position. Clear the text and blur again: the label returns inside the field.

aspects.description: A progress bar is fixed at the top of the viewport on the provided page
aspects.extraDescription: Test: Open A2 (based on assets/A2/index.html). A bar is visible in a fixed position at the top of the viewport. No JavaScript is used for the effect.

aspects.description: Progress bar width is 0% when the page is scrolled to the top
aspects.extraDescription: Test: Scroll to the very top. The bar width is 0% (not filled).

aspects.description: Progress bar reaches 100% at the bottom and follows scroll in between
aspects.extraDescription: Test: Scroll through the page. The bar grows with scroll position and is 100% wide at the bottom.

aspects.description: The can is displayed in the centre with the wrapper on top
aspects.extraDescription: Test: Open A3. A can is centred on the screen. The wrapper image (assets/A3/wrapping.png) sits on top of the can mockup (assets/A3/can-mockup.png). HTML/CSS only.

aspects.description: Page background uses the specified radial gradient
aspects.extraDescription: Test: Inspect computed/background CSS. Background is radial-gradient(at 50%, #081718 -20%, #28aeb4 90%) or a visually matching equivalent.

aspects.description: The wrapper is correctly applied to the can
aspects.extraDescription: Test: Compare with assets/A3/example.mov. The wrapping graphic follows the can shape (masked or mapped onto the mockup), not a flat rectangle beside it.

aspects.description: Hovering the can plays the rotation and scaling animation
aspects.extraDescription: Test: Hover the can. It rotates and scales as in the example video. The effect is CSS-only (no JavaScript).

aspects.description: All buildings from the provided data are rendered on the page
aspects.extraDescription: Test: Open B1. Five towers from assets/B1/buildings.js appear: Burj Khalifa, Merdeka 118, Canton Tower, Taipei 101, Oriental Pearl Tower, using the images in assets/B1/towers/.

aspects.description: Buildings are aligned to the bottom of the page as a skyline
aspects.extraDescription: Test: The towers stand side by side with their bases on a common bottom line (bottom of the page/viewport).

aspects.description: Buildings are sorted tallest-first and scaled with the tallest at 800px
aspects.extraDescription: Test: Left-to-right (or document order) is tallest first: Burj Khalifa (828 m) is 800px tall. Others keep aspect ratio and scale by height/828 (Merdeka 118 ≈ 656px, Canton Tower ≈ 584px, Taipei 101 ≈ 491px, Oriental Pearl ≈ 452px). Allow a few pixels of rounding.

aspects.description: Pressing the platter starts playback of a provided audio track
aspects.extraDescription: Test: Open B2 (starter HTML/CSS/images/audio). Click .wheel. One of DrunkonSoju.wav or LostSomewhere.wav starts playing. No server is required.

aspects.description: Platter rotates while the song is playing
aspects.extraDescription: Test: Start playback. The platter (.wheel) rotates, matching assets/B2/video/turntable.mp4.

aspects.description: Tone-arm moves above the platter while the song is playing
aspects.extraDescription: Test: Start playback. The tone-arm moves over the platter as in the reference video.

aspects.description: Off button stops the song and returns platter and tone-arm to the rest state
aspects.extraDescription: Test: Start playback, then click Off. Audio stops. Platter rotation and tone-arm return to the original rest state.

aspects.description: Volume control ranges from 0 to 1 and changes the playback volume
aspects.extraDescription: Test: While a track plays, move the volume range. Min is 0, max is 1. Audible level changes with the control.

aspects.description: Next button switches to the other provided audio track
aspects.extraDescription: Test: Play a track, then click >>. Playback switches between DrunkonSoju.wav and LostSomewhere.wav.

aspects.description: When a song ends, the tone-arm returns to its original state
aspects.extraDescription: Test: Seek near the end of a track or wait until it finishes. The tone-arm animation returns to the rest position.

aspects.description: Forty dots appear with random position, size, and colour from the provided array
aspects.extraDescription: Test: Open B3 (starter in assets/B3/index.html). Count about 40 dots. Colours are from ["#47C2E3", "#FEC85B", "#0064A8", "#1cc8cf"]. Reload: positions, sizes, and colours randomise again.

aspects.description: Moving the cursor produces the lines-and-dots animation from the example video
aspects.extraDescription: Test: Move the pointer around the page. Lines and dots react as in assets/B3/example.mov (no server required).

aspects.description: Form loads with empty fields and no validation feedback
aspects.extraDescription: Test: php -S localhost:8080 from C1 (or the submission root). Open the form. First name, Last name, and the checkbox are empty/unchecked. No “Looks good!” or error messages are shown yet.

aspects.description: Server-side name validation uses a–z/A–Z only and the required messages
aspects.extraDescription: Test: Submit first name “Jane” and last name “1234”. Valid field shows “Looks good!”. Invalid field shows “Please provide a valid name.”. Repeat with a POST of invalid data (curl or DevTools) to confirm rejection is server-side, not only HTML required/pattern.

aspects.description: Unchecked checkbox shows the required message; all-valid submit displays Success
aspects.extraDescription: Test: Valid names, checkbox off → “You must agree before submitting.”. Valid names plus checked checkbox → page displays “Success”.

aspects.description: Endpoint accepts POST with Content-Type application/json
aspects.extraDescription: Test: php -S from C2. POST the URL from README.txt with header Content-Type: application/json and body {"message":"hello"}. Response is success (2xx).

aspects.description: Each accepted call is stored in a separate file in the log folder
aspects.extraDescription: Test: Send two successful POSTs. Two distinct new files appear in the log folder named in README.txt.

aspects.description: Log file name uses the HH-MM-SS-request.txt format
aspects.extraDescription: Test: Compare the new file name to the time of the POST. It matches HH-MM-SS-request.txt (hour-minute-second, hyphens, not colons).

aspects.description: Stored log file contains the received JSON payload
aspects.extraDescription: Test: Open the file created by the hello POST. It contains the JSON body (at least {"message":"hello"}).

aspects.description: Non-POST or non-JSON requests are rejected with an appropriate HTTP status
aspects.extraDescription: Test: GET the endpoint → 4xx/405. POST with Content-Type text/plain (or no JSON type) → 4xx/415. No new success log file is created for those calls.

aspects.description: README.txt documents the URL to call and where log files are stored
aspects.extraDescription: Test: Open C2/README.txt. It states the URL (or path) to POST and the folder where HH-MM-SS-request.txt files are written.
